https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Record liveness failures in a cancellation-safe way so trigger_liveness_close still fires.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: If an outer timeout cancels the future mid-retry, a match arm never runs; recording earlier means the liveness counter still increments.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Forward a writable TMPDIR into the aarch64 cross test container.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Lib tests panicked in the aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu cross job because the container lacked a writable temp dir.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Make read_to_end fail with an error when chunks are missing instead of returning zero-filled data.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: ReadToEnd filled a zeroed buffer and returned Ok even with gaps, which showed up as 1448-byte zero windows in gossip; unsigned consumers would ingest that corruption silently.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Release the endpoint UDP socket on explicit shutdown by swapping it for an ephemeral loopback socket
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: The QUIC socket is no longer kept alive by the default transport registry, so the same fixed port can be re-bound right away even while the endpoint handle still exists.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Update dependencies to fix RUSTSEC-2026-0190 (anyhow undefined behaviour) and RUSTSEC-2026-0185 (stream reassembly DoS)
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: These advisories failed the daily security workflow; patched versions remove the anyhow UB and the out-of-order stream reassembly denial of service.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Replace the last unchecked time subtraction in ant-quic with a checked one and add a boot-epoch test
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Subtracting Instants can panic if the clock value is earlier than expected, such as right after boot; checked math makes the time code panic-free.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Detect overlapping stream chunk data that disagrees, and add content verification tests
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Overlapping received chunks whose bytes differ point to data corruption; checking them catches it instead of silently passing bad data on.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Release connection state of failed sessions promptly.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Failed dials held about 2.3 MB each; freeing the session holder early cuts that memory.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Allocate per-stream state lazily instead of for every stream MAX_STREAMS allows
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: StreamsState::new used to insert a HashMap entry for every allowed remote stream up front, costing megabytes per connection even if no stream opened; creating entries on demand removes that cost.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Return an error when the stream assembler holds too many gaps
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Capping the number of out-of-order chunks per stream stops a remote peer from exhausting memory; this is security advisory GHSA-4w2j-m93h-cj5j.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Treat transient ICMP-derived recv errors as non-fatal in the endpoint driver.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: One ICMP-unreachable peer could end the only driver task and silently stop all QUIC I/O, and the bootstrap cache re-dialled that peer first after restart.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Raise the rustls minimum version to 0.23.40
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: rustls::crypto::aws_lc_rs::kx_group::MLKEM1024 first appears in 0.23.40, so the higher floor stops Cargo from picking a rustls that lacks it.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Make dial_addr never hang for bare endpoints and demux accept() by protocol.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Fixes two defects: dial_addr could hang on a bare endpoint, and accept() did not separate incoming connections by protocol.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Kill connections with no ACK progress, bound the recv event channel and cap connection count.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: on_packet_authenticated reset the idle timer for every packet, so a peer that keeps sending but never ACKs never timed out and zombies pinned memory.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Make the ADR gate recognise ## Status records and check Accepted ADRs against their history.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: History-based snapshots catch edits, status rollback, deletion, rename and net-zero branch changes that a base-relative check missed.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Update the lifecycle state and winner map under one lock so connection replacement is atomic.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Releasing the lock early let two concurrent dials both mark a connection Live and write the map out of order, and could leave a stale connected peer.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Stop charging packets from abandoned paths to the surviving path when they are acked or lost
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Connection::remove_in_flight picked a path only by its first packet number, so packets of a dropped path were debited from the current one; attributing them correctly prevents the underflow.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Report the real transport close reason when the reader task exits
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Showing the actual close reason instead of a generic ReaderExit makes it possible to see why a connection ended.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Let received application payload reset the idle timer.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: An earlier change only reset the idle timer on ACK progress while unacked data was held, so active connections could time out.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Treat transient UdpSender::poll_send errors as non-fatal in State::drive_transmit.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Every non-WouldBlock send error killed the connection driver; a temporary error should not end the connection.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Reset an unfinished SendStream on drop instead of finishing it
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Finishing on drop made a partly written stream look complete to the peer. Resetting signals the data is incomplete.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Finish the relay send stream at a frame boundary when the client cleanly half-closes
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: The forwarding loop treated every read-side exit as a failure and reset the reverse stream, losing complete but unacknowledged frames. A clean half-close now finishes the stream instead.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Isolate the upsert_peer_hints tests from the machine bootstrap cache
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: The tests no longer read the real on-disk cache, so leftover peers on a developer machine cannot change their result.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Close open connections that have no reader to stop a memory leak
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: A connection with no reader never drains, so its receive Assembler pins every inbound datagram up to the 16 MiB window. LAN churn creates many such orphans, so memory kept growing.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Keep the connection reader running when a single stream has a read error
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: A read error scoped to one stream was killing the whole connection reader, hurting throughput; stream errors now stay on that stream.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Seed connection-local NAT candidates and make traversal counters honest
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Adding the connection's own local candidates helps hole punching, and counters now report real traversal attempts.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Grant relay/coordinator capability only from outbound-verified direct connections, not inbound accepts
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Inbound accepts recorded a NATed peer's source address as global reachability, so every NATed desktop dialling a bootstrap was marked a relay. Inbound addresses are now only redial candidates (observe_inbound_peer_address).

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Use the MASQUE relay as the guaranteed last fallback for connections, with an end-to-end test
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: When direct and hole-punched connections fail, the relay path is now always tried, so peers behind NAT can still connect.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Cap handshake padding and keep the path MTU at 1200 bytes until probing confirms more
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: PQC handshake and path-validation padding made 4096-byte UDP datagrams that relied on IP fragmentation, which often fails. Large handshake data is now split across multiple CRYPTO datagrams, as RFC 9000 section 14 expects.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Bind exactly to an explicit non-wildcard P2pConfig.bind_addr instead of falling back to a wildcard
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: The dual-stack binder kept only the port, so 127.0.0.1:0 could become a wildcard IPv6 socket and advertise an unusable address to x0x. The requested IP is now honored.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Make a peer invisible to lookups as soon as disconnect() starts, before teardown finishes
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: New streams can no longer pick up a connection that is closing, so callers fall back to a fresh connection.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Fix tiebreaker liveness, promotion visibility and finalize staleness in ant-quic
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Connection tiebreak and promotion logic could stall or act on stale state; these changes keep both sides agreeing.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Allow only one accept_bi consumer per connection
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: With two readers calling accept_bi on the same connection, one could take a stream the other was waiting for; a single consumer stops streams from being lost.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Close superseded connections explicitly before releasing the socket on shutdown
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Their CONNECTION_CLOSE frames now get sent while the socket is still alive, so the remote sees the close straight away.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Join accept workers on shutdown and refuse handshake registrations that arrive late
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Waiting for the workers and rejecting registrations after shutdown starts means no new connection can slip into the maps after cleanup.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Keep the full connection deadline for address-only connect_addr dials
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Address-only dials no longer abort at the 2.082s Happy Eyeballs stage budget, so slow but valid handshakes can finish within the 30s connection deadline.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Reserve time for relay fallback within the connection deadline and abort Happy Eyeballs attempts on drop; require Rustls 0.23.45
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Address-only dials could spend the whole deadline before relay fallback, and leftover attempts kept running; the Rustls pin fixes RUSTSEC-2026-0285.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Close the connection, wake waiters and drop the route when a UDP send fails fatally
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: A non-transient send error ended the driver but left the connection reported as live and its waiters stuck forever.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Stop logging WARN on every P2pEndpoint::send to an unconnected peer (EndpointError::PeerNotFound)
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Sending to a peer with no live connection is normal when membership views lag, but each one logged a WARN and filled disks (about 16 GB of syslog a day).

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Release hole-punch dials, session and relay handles and queued streams on shutdown
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Those handles were holding references to the UDP socket; dropping them lets the socket be freed. Shipped in 0.27.55.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Release the remaining socket holders on shutdown
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Freeing the last handles that referenced the socket stops the remaining weak_socket_owner_still_live failures. Shipped in 0.27.56.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Do the hole-punch winner check and insert under the lifecycle lock
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Concurrent hole-punch winners for the same peer could both pass the check and both be inserted. Holding the lock makes check and insert one atomic step.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Start a reader task for raw coordinator and hole-punch winner connections
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Winning connections from coordination or hole punching had no reader, so their incoming data was never consumed. Retiring old connections is left for later.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Make the tests do genuine reconnects and check the cross-family tiebreak directly
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Test-only change: the reconnect tests now really open a new connection instead of reusing the live one, and the tiebreak is asserted directly.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Accept reordered reads, legal datagrams and contiguous chunks on the receive path
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Three receive-path bugs from a forward-port rejected data the peer is allowed to send. The checks were corrected; the advertised datagram limit is unchanged.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Use OS-assigned ports in the port binding tests instead of fixed ones
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Each test gets a free port, with bounded retries for the release-and-rebind race, so overlapping runs no longer clash.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Check max_datagram_frame_size against the whole encoded DATAGRAM frame, per RFC 9221
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: The limit covers frame type, optional length varint and payload, and a value of 0 means DATAGRAM frames are not supported. Breaking either rule is now treated as a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Map CLOSE_CODE_NO_READER to ConnectionCloseReason::NoReader in from_app_error_code
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: The close code now converts to the right reason, and tests cover every close code the endpoint sends.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Read the current local peer ID right before registering inbound connections
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Accept loops now share the id updated by set_local_peer_id instead of a stale copy, covering both constructors, start_listening and the relay accept loop.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Reuse the OS-assigned IPv6 port for the IPv4 bind in the no-default-features fallback
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Both address families now share one port; if that fails it binds v6-only, because local_addr() prefers IPv6 and a different v4 port leaves IPv4 dials undeliverable.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Send each lifecycle event to both streams while holding one lock
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: With both sends under one lock, no other event can slip in between, so both streams see the same order.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Correct the docs so they no longer overstate what the bounded worker join guarantees
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: The drain had already been moved inside the connection_lifecycle.write() critical section; this change only makes the docs match.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Allow QUIC service ports 80, 443 and 853 in NAT candidate validation and expire address verdicts
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Reusing the existing QUIC port allowlist lets these candidates form pairs, while port zero, other privileged ports and invalid addresses are still rejected.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Add a test that races two reader starts for the same connection
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: The bug was already fixed: start_reader now reserves the single reader slot under the reader_handles write lock before spawning, so a duplicate start spawns nothing.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Add a deterministic test for a coordinator replacing a hole-punch winner while another candidate waits
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: It checks the late candidate is closed as a duplicate, the coordinator stays Live, and the displaced winner stays tracked as Superseded until its stream completes.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Add a test for an inbound reconnect while a dead connection is still marked Live
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: The fixes were already in: dead connections cannot win the tiebreak, surviving connections are promoted back, and stale peer records are rejected; the test guards that path.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Rebuild the benchmark PR gate so it stops reporting false performance regressions
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: PRs now compare allowlisted ant-quic bench ids on the same runner against the merge-base, with a same-commit control. A regression needs non-overlapping 95% Criterion confidence intervals, not a raw mean difference.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Count a relay connection attempt when try_relay_connection starts
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Relay-only connections could show nat_traversal_successes = 1 with nat_traversal_attempts = 0; counting at entry includes failed attempts too.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Add a regression test for redialing a host that still holds a stale connection
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: The bug was already fixed; the test (regression_235_stale_redial) checks that repeated redials complete the handshake and replace the stale handle.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Reuse an existing live IPv4 connection to a peer when using dual-stack sockets
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: On a dual-stack socket the live connection to a relay peer is now reused instead of opening another. Later steps (supersede arbitration, reader handover) are left for separate work.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Fix the product bug behind the flaky raw_winner_adoption_is_reader_only test
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: The test sometimes panicked with "a reader adoption must not record an outer peer" on macOS, Ubuntu and Windows CI. The cause was a real bug in the code, not test ordering, so the code was fixed rather than the test.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Keep the direct handshake running after the hole-punch cutoff instead of aborting it
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: A PeerId dial starts hole punching at the cutoff but the direct attempt keeps racing, all bounded by the caller's deadline, so a slow direct handshake can still win.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Stop queueing NatTraversalEvents when nobody polls them, with a small cap as backstop
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Events nobody consumed piled up in memory; they are now only kept for users who drive NatTraversalEndpoint::poll(), and a bounded cap limits growth.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Rewrite the supersede close test so it always creates a real losing connection
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: The old test's redials reused the live connection, leaving nothing to observe closing, and it did not wait for the inbound reader to start.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Bump rustls-webpki and webpki roots in Cargo.lock
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Updating the lockfile to patched versions clears the advisories without other code changes.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Reject oversized Retry tokens, porting the quinn-proto 0.11.19 fix for GHSA-wppq-2f6r-wfvm
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: A Retry packet with a very long token could panic the client or exhaust its memory. Oversized tokens are now rejected.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Lock saorsa-pqc 0.5.2 and tokio 1.53.3 to fix RUSTSEC-2026-0387 and another RustSec advisory
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: RUSTSEC-2026-0387 reports crypto-bigint constant-time operations could branch on secrets; only crypto-bigint 0.7.6+ is patched. The new locks pull in fixed versions so the Vulnerability Scan passes.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Treat missing tokens on fork pull requests as a skip, not a job failure
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: GitHub withholds OIDC and write scopes on fork pull_request runs; the jobs keep minimal scopes and no longer fail when the token is withheld, without switching to pull_request_target.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.fix: Expose the connection generation on accepted and opened app streams
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/.how: Apps can now tell which connection a stream came from when old and new connections to a peer exist at once.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/communita.fix: Update dependencies to resolve RUSTSEC-2026-0193, RUSTSEC-2026-0185, RUSTSEC-2026-0190 and RUSTSEC-2026-0173
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/communita.how: These advisories were failing the daily cargo security audit workflow; moving to patched versions makes it pass.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/communita.fix: Update dependencies to resolve RUSTSEC-2026-0213, 0204, 0257 and 0253, and ignore the yrs smallstr advisory
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/communita.how: Fixes failing nightly Security Audit and Dependency License Audit jobs.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/communita.fix: Replace previous sizes in storage stats when a file is overwritten instead of adding them again.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/communita.how: LocalStorageManager now captures the previous entry so personal, shard and DHT stats are not double counted.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.fix: Move audio commands off Tokio worker threads.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.how: Audio commands can block, so running them off the async workers keeps the runtime responsive.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.fix: Track silent proactive generation separately so it does not leave the UI stuck in Thinking.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.how: An AssistantGenerationTracker separates visible Thinking from silent background work and stops superseded turns from bringing Thinking back.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.fix: Allow expect/unwrap in tests so the Linux render spike clippy step passes.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.how: The lint step treated expect/unwrap in test code as errors; allowing them in tests turns the job green.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.fix: Fix six real bugs and six wrong assertions in auto-generated coverage tests to repair the macOS Tests gate.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.how: The failures were 12 real assertion failures, not an MLX crash; the generated tests had never been checked against the gate before reaching main.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.fix: Make the memory-recall rule conditional so the model recalls from memory instead of calling tools
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.how: The model over-reached on personal-recall turns, calling contacts or web_search when answering from memory was correct; the prompt rule now says when to use recall.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.fix: Reclaim an orphaned llama-server sidecar on startup after fae-daemon dies uncleanly
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.how: After a crash or SIGKILL the sidecar was left running and holding port 18080, causing a crash-loop or a stale engine on the next launch; startup now cleans it up.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.fix: Allow FAE_MODELS_LOCK_PATH only in dev builds and measure the TTS limit in characters, not bytes
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.how: The models lock override could bypass the integrity gate, so it is now dev-only. The TTS length bound mixed chars and bytes, which miscounted multi-byte text.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.fix: Suppress auto-replies to peer envelopes flagged by trust_decision and log a security event
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.how: Envelopes marked for quarantine were still answered automatically; the transport layer now enforces the quarantine.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.fix: Wire the OpenRouter route to RemoteAllowed so it can actually be reached
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.how: The conductor routing had no path to RemoteAllowed, so that route was dead code; connecting it makes the remote route usable.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.fix: Clear the stranded assistantGenerating flag so the UI no longer gets stuck on Thinking after proactive turns
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.how: A pipeline state bug left the generating flag set after a proactive turn; resetting it lets the state return to idle.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.fix: Log a warning when the OpenRouter environment settings are incomplete
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.how: It only adds observability; cloud routing decisions stay fail-closed and unchanged when the key is complete, missing or the lane is disabled.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.fix: Add a diagnostic recipe to identify stale Fae sidecar processes
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.how: It is a headless, owner-run maintenance check only; automatic sidecar ownership and reclaim behaviour stays unchanged and fails closed.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.fix: Turn on the ADR lifecycle governance CI workflow with its validator and tests.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/fae/pull/.how: CI-only change that enforces ADR status rules; no app code is touched.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: Subscribers cannot see the validated MessageHeader.msg_id of a received message
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: Delivery returns only (PeerId, Bytes); hashing the payload is not the same, since two sends with identical bytes have different ids.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: A local Normal publish can be skipped for every peer and waits 30s for anti-entropy
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: Per-peer permits held by relay traffic block all claims, and no lazy announcement is sent.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: A peer stays suppressed on a topic forever when its recovery probe's permit is refused
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: The probe in-flight flag is never cleared when the send permit is denied.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: HyParView active view keeps peers that were never connected
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: Random-walk peers enter the active view without a transport connection and nothing prunes them, causing a log flood of about 16 GB/day.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: An IWANT reply whose claim was pruned can leave a recovery probe stuck
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: The serve arms a probe that neither its stale completion nor its drop guard can clear.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: Passing StrategyConfig::default() disables hole punching and relay for that dial
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: udp_transport_adapter.rs calls connect_with_fallback with an explicit default strategy, which has no coordinator and no relays.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: Replaying a payload under a new message ID bypasses the validator's Drop
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: Replay suppression returns before validation, so the replayed copy is cached as serveable over IWANT.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: warn! and error! logs print raw peer identifiers
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: After switching the fleet to RUST_LOG=warn to cut log volume, identifiers in warning and error logs still need to be salted hashes for privacy.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: UdpTransportAdapter::close() leaves the ant-quic connections open
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: It clears its peer map but never closes the underlying QUIC connections.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: GossipRuntime peer_id differs from the transport's peer_id when no identity is set
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: GossipRuntimeBuilder makes a fresh MlDsaKeyPair if none is given, even if the transport was built with another keypair via with_keypair.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: dropped_critical_hard_error keeps rising when Critical messages go to the same peer at once
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: The counter must stay zero in production, but concurrent Critical sends to one peer still drop after the dedicated Critical lane fix.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: Critical sends to a cooled peer are silently dropped
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: Cooling is skipped for Critical at the admission layer but not at the claim/gate layer, which starves membership and Welcome traffic and breaks group convergence under load.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: stop_beacons() leaves the beacon task running after its 5s timeout
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: On timeout it returns Err but drops the JoinHandle instead of aborting, so a beacon mid-broadcast can outlive the caller's shutdown.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: Anchor nodes back up under fanout bursts because pubsub handlers are serialised
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: Under a burst, 97% of handler time went to two stages behind a global topics write lock.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: publish_local reaches zero peers but returns Ok(()) and logs only at trace
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: Callers cannot tell an undelivered publish from a delivered one, and peer cooling can remove every eligible peer for a topic.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: Pre-commit hook fails on clean main because cargo hakari verify exits 1
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: Failing with no changes teaches contributors to skip the hook with --no-verify.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: x0xd hangs on SIGTERM because spawn_ihave_flusher cannot be stopped
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: The IHAVE flusher has no shutdown handle and livelocks all workers after the transport shuts down.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: Pubsub validators cannot forward relayed messages lazily without losing delivery
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: The verdicts either eager-forward or withhold the IHAVE too, so a subscriber behind a relay learns nothing.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.applies_when: saorsa-gossip pubsub topic validators, relay nodes

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: Bulk-priority topics never recover from peer cooling
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: After cooling expires the leftover suppression state makes admit_bulk drop the send, so the recovery probe is never reached.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: Dedupe concurrency test does not check that the overlap it relies on happened
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: Asserting verify.count >= 2 would pin the concurrency the test depends on.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.problem: Proptest membership::pending_probes_cleared_on_ack fails at random in CI
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.detail: The same commit passes and fails across different CI runs.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Keep EAGER forwarding going after one send failure, and prune stale peers with set_topic_peers.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: One send_to_peer error used to abort the whole loop via ?; now it is logged and the rest are still sent, and disconnected peers are removed.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Announce claim-skipped local publishes within one flush, add a local-origin permit and fix the probe-flag leak
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: Skipped publishes now get announced quickly instead of waiting for anti-entropy, local publishes are not starved by relay permits, and a refused permit clears the probe flag.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Keep the validator's refusal when the same payload is replayed
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: A payload the validator dropped stays unserveable even if rewrapped under a fresh outer message ID.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Pass no strategy so ant-quic chooses the NAT fallback strategy itself
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: An explicit strategy is authoritative in ant-quic and skips filling in coordinator and relays; leaving it out lets the dial use hole punching and relay.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Prune disconnected peers from the active view and refill it from the passive view
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: SWIM, shuffles and forward-JOINs no longer keep sending to unreachable peer ids.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Check the exact reply token under the send-attempt lock before claiming attempts or permits
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: Missing or replaced claims now return no attempts, so no probe is armed that cannot be cleared.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Add subscribe_with_msg_id APIs that deliver the authenticated msg_id with each message
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: A new SubscriptionMessage carries the msg_id only after header authentication, never a payload hash; old subscribe channels and the wire format are unchanged.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Let Critical Data through claim-layer cooling
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: Critical claims no longer return None for a cooled peer, matching admission's always-admit rule, and they are sent as Normal attempts so they do not use the cooldown-bypass slot.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Disconnect every live ant-quic connection in UdpTransportAdapter close() before clearing tracking maps.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: close() only cleared local maps, so the node stayed reachable on the wire; calling Node::disconnect() for each Node::connected_peers() entry gives real shutdown.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Start SwimDetector timers with interval_at(now + period, period) so the first tick is one period later.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: tokio::time::interval fires immediately on spawn, so the probe task could re-insert a peer into pending_probes right after an ack, making pending_probes_cleared_on_ack flaky.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Enforce that GossipRuntime and its transport use the same peer id
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: Before, build() could create a runtime whose peer_id() differed from the transport, so pubsub routed to one id while the transport delivered under another and sends failed.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Promote lazy peers back to eager on set_topic_peers refresh and add a gossip keepalive.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: Peers pruned during message bursts stayed lazy forever and broke PlumTree routing; send_ping() and all_topic_ids() let relay nodes keep and refresh peer sets.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Shard the topics map, fix republish timing attribution and instrument mutexes
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: Sharding removes the single write lock that serialised all handlers, and the instrumentation shows where other global locks still block.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Use ant-quic's full NAT traversal fallback in dial(): direct, then hole-punch, then MASQUE relay.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: dial() only tried Node::connect_addr() once, so peers behind symmetric NAT failed silently.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Split benign no-target Critical control drops out of dropped_critical_hard_error.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: The counter must stay zero, but it mixed real errors with harmless drops when there was no target, tripping x0x's convergence soak gate.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Trust the live transport connection over a stale SWIM health snapshot when sending.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: The SWIM snapshot could still say Suspect or Dead after a new QUIC connection, so Normal traffic was silently dropped to a connected peer.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Expose zero-fanout publishes and always keep one eligible eager peer for local topics
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: A new publish_with_fanout API returns the fan-out count, zero-target publishes log WARN and bump zero_fanout_publishes, and the kept peer stops cooling from black-holing all publishes.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Refuse to forward gossip payloads that end in a zeroed tail.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: Forwarding corrupt payloads spread them to other peers; the guard stops relays from passing the damage on.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Detect interior zero windows in payloads before forwarding, not only zero tails.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: The tail-only guard never fired; most live corruption was zero runs inside messages with intact tails.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Regenerate the workspace-hack crate so cargo hakari verify passes on clean main
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: An up-to-date workspace-hack makes the verify step pass, so the hook's other checks run again.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Evict not-connected peers on send instead of putting them on cooldown
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: A send to a peer that is no longer connected now removes it, so dead peers do not linger and keep being retried.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Stop cooling peers when the local outbound budget is exhausted
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: Budget exhaustion means this node is saturated, not that the peer misbehaved. Cooling peers for it caused a loop that kept the gossip storm going.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Raise PER_PEER_REPUBLISH_TIMEOUT from 750 ms to 2500 ms.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: On long public internet paths under load, sends exceeded 750 ms, so healthy peers were counted as timed out and suppressed.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Recover publishes that reached no eager peer using a self-IHAVE and bounded retry
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: If every eager send failed, the message had no pull path because all-eager topics have no lazy members to receive IHAVE, so it was stranded.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Drop duplicate inbound EAGER messages before running the ML-DSA-65 signature check
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: Verifying every duplicate wasted CPU on expensive post-quantum checks; deduplicating first skips them. No wire format change.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Add ValidationAction::LazyForward that delivers and caches but announces only via IHAVE
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: The relay skips the eager re-publish but announces the msg_id to lazy peers and withheld eager peers, cutting CPU while subscribers can still fetch the message.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Replace a cooled peer instead of only dropping it, and make the Bulk recovery probe reachable
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: With a max eager degree of 2, one timeout left the topic at degree 1 for the 120 s cooldown or longer, because suppression cleared only on a recovery probe that could not run.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Use a read lock for the pre-verify dedupe check in handle_eager_admitted
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: It took the per-topic write lock just for a read-only has_message lookup, adding contention on every inbound message.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Give gossip background tasks a shutdown path so the IHAVE flusher stops after transport shutdown
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: spawn_ihave_flusher and its siblings used tokio::spawn loops with dropped JoinHandles and no cancel token, so they kept spinning after shutdown.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Bound per-topic peer state, peer_scores_v2 and the pending-IHAVE queue
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: These structures could grow without limit; caps stop memory growth.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Allow a rate-limited cooldown bypass while a peer is actively suppressed
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: Cooled peers could stay out of the mesh too long; a limited bypass lets them be used again when needed.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Assert verify.count >= 2 in the dedupe concurrency test
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: The test now fails if the concurrent verification it depends on did not actually overlap.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Abort and reap the beacon task when it outlives the 5s grace period
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: Aborting instead of detaching the task guarantees no beacon keeps running after stop_beacons() returns.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Repair cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo hakari verify failures on main.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: Main was red after merges, and since PR CI tests against merged main, every open PR was blocked until main was fixed.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Admit recovery intents fairly and allow displacement instead of first-come-first-served
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: When full, LeafEgressLimiter refused new IHAVE/IWANT targets with ReserveError::IntentLimit for up to 120 s regardless of budget, starving busy relays.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.fix: Remove dispatch overhead when the leaf limiter is disabled and bound late-offer catch-up
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-go.how: A new release raised failed DM pairs about 2.5 times on relays with the limiter disabled; skipping the extra work restores delivery.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-ml.fix: Run cargo fmt and add missing CI files (.tsan-suppressions.txt, examples directory).
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-ml.how: Workflows failed on formatting and on files the ThreadSanitizer and benchmark jobs expected to exist.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-ml.fix: Remove if: conditions that test secrets for emptiness in GitHub Actions workflows.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-ml.how: Checks like if: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN != '' }} are invalid and caused workflow parse errors.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-ml.fix: Make the cargo-deny license check non-blocking.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-ml.how: The license check was failing the whole Security Audit workflow.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-ml.fix: Ignore RUSTSEC-2023-0089 (atomic-polyfill) and drop the stale RUSTSEC-2025-0134 entry in cargo-deny.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-ml.how: atomic-polyfill comes in via postcard 1.x and heapless 0.7 with no newer postcard release yet, and the old ignore no longer matched any crate.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-ml.fix: Use valid SPDX license identifiers in the dependency review config.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-ml.how: The Dependency Review check failed on every PR because of invalid SPDX identifiers.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-pq.fix: Stop DudeCT timing tests from writing one line per sample and filling the CI runner disk
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-pq.how: The weekly constant-time test failures were the runner running out of disk, not a timing leak or code change. Limiting the transcript output keeps the job within disk space.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-pq.fix: Clear new RustSec advisories at the source instead of adding them to the ignore list.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-pq.how: Security Checks went red on an unchanged Cargo.lock as new advisories were published.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-pq.fix: Release 0.5.2 from a clean tag and verify the packaged source and crates.io checksum before publishing.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-pq.how: 0.5.1 was published from a dirty tree; binding releases to a clean v* tag and checking artifacts makes them reproducible and reruns safe.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-ro.fix: Apply quality improvements to the camera integration code.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-ro.how: Follow-up fixes for the camera integration; the text gives no specific detail.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/tic-tac-t.problem: Desktop history_get always misses because GET /history/message/:msg_id does not exist
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/tic-tac-t.detail: x0xd 0.37.1/0.37.2 has no such route; the client turns the 404 into None, so redelivery and point checks treat every lookup as a miss.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/tic-tac-t.problem: Shipped app bundles an unreleased x0xd build and cannot DM the real network
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/tic-tac-t.detail: The bundled x0xd is a campaign-branch build labelled 0.37.0 with unreleased durable-ACK behaviour.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/tic-tac-t.fix: Pass the history scope query to GET /history/message
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/tic-tac-t.how: Canonical group ids need ?scope= to resolve; without it lookups still returned 404 once the route existed.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/tic-tac-t.fix: Pin the bundled x0xd to the official 0.37.2 release
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/tic-tac-t.how: The branch build made POST /direct/send fail with 409 recipient_ack_semantics_unavailable against real peers; the official release matches the fleet.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/tic-tac-t.fix: Ship the v0.5.1 rebrand, working contacts and DMs, and stop signing 17-byte agent placeholders.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/tic-tac-t.how: This product slice removes old branding, a dead contact UI and placeholder agent signing so a v0.5.1 DMG can ship.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ttt/pull/.fix: Use the macos-15-intel runner label instead of the retired macos-13 for x64 release builds
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ttt/pull/.how: GitHub retired macos-13, but jobs asking for it wait forever instead of failing, so the release workflow stayed queued and never published.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-nostr.problem: The NIP-11 relay info document has no active unit test.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-nostr.detail: The endpoint is served but untested, so supported_nips or the document shape can break without notice.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-nostr.fix: Add CORS support so browser clients on another origin can call the bridge.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-nostr.how: Browser calls with an X-Pubkey header and JSON body trigger a CORS preflight, which failed without CORS headers.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-nostr.fix: Evaluate every generic tag filter in to_filter_spec, not only #h, #e and #p.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-nostr.how: The catch-all arm in src/history_adapter.rs ignored other tags, so filters on them did not work.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-nostr.fix: Key the 39006 d tag on the request cursor and seed the general channel by uuid5.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-nostr.how: Both changes are needed: fixing only the channel seeding still left the parity test at zero rows.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-nostr.fix: Add the HTTP dialect and WebSocket/auth hardening on top of the real HistoryStore, with tests.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-nostr.how: Integrating these work packages over the real history store covers the NIP-11 and related gaps with active tests.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-symph.problem: A locally created issue is marked network_sourced and blocked, but missing from pending approvals.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-symph.detail: With x0x-symphony v0.1.2 and x0xd v0.32.0, a task from x0x-symphony issue new is rebuilt as issue_source: network_sourced, so it can neither run nor be approved.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-symph.problem: Built-in pi and claude_code runner presets fail CLI argument parsing.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-symph.detail: The presets in x0x-symphony v0.1.2 pass arguments the current installed harnesses reject.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-symph.fix: Pin the pi, claude_code and codex preset argv to the real CLI argument contracts.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-symph.how: Matching the arguments each installed CLI actually accepts stops the parse failures; codex had the same problem.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-symph.fix: Dispatch local self-signed issues under all policies and show awaiting-approval issues so they can be approved.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x-symph.how: Self-signed local issues are recognised as local, and issues needing approval are now visible and approvable instead of stuck.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: ShareGrant outbox keeps expired entries on disk and the reconnect nudge skips already-due entries
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: Expired entries are not rewritten on load and due entries are left out of the nudge.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: DM capability upgrade is lost at startup, so cross-NAT DMs fail
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: watch::Sender::send drops the value when no receiver is subscribed yet, so the advert stays non-gossip-ready and peers fall back to raw QUIC, which fails across NAT.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Home admission deadlocks with OwnerCertMemberPending when the creator device is offline
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The admin's view of the creator stays digest-only, so it cannot get the owner cert while the creator is offline.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x Home with the creator/owner device offline

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: x0xd floods syslog with ant_quic::send_error 'send failed' WARN, about 16 GB a day, filling disks
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The warning logged so often in production that it filled a node's disk to 100%.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0xd in production on Linux with syslog

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: A restarted owner device refuses its own enrolled owner machine's SyncV1 stream, so Home provisioning stalls
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: After restart the discovery cache is empty, and the check relied on it, denying an authenticated enrolled machine.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x owner sync after a device restart

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: KV direct-delivery fallback never delivers: serde_json fails with 'key must be a string'
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: KvStoreDelta has maps with non-string keys, which serde_json cannot encode.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Unenrolling an owner device leaves no tombstone and live SyncV1 sessions keep running
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: Live sessions are not re-checked after unenroll, a limitation documented in ADR 0084.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Promoted group admins cannot actually administer private groups
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: Admin invites and changes are rejected or do not converge, and ownership transfer is unsupported, despite role rules in state_commit.rs.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: The e2e_deploy.sh log-cap step breaks logrotate

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: S4 delivery can close a group seat without checking the current live roster.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The delivery completion step relied on older state, so it could close a seat that the live roster no longer agrees with.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x named groups, S4 delivery completion

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: After readmission, a joiner loops in catching_up / rate_limited with no group keys.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: After readmission from readmission_required {base_beyond_retention}, the joiner holds only a signer_only marker for a seal and its Welcome fetch times out once the admin holding it is released.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x named groups, readmission after base_beyond_retention

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: An Active group member cannot republish a fresh KEM key without leaving and re-joining.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: Rotating the member's KEM (key encapsulation) key required a full re-join.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x named groups, KEM key rotation

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Catch-up, control-blob and seat-cert answers never reach a device whose machine was revoked.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: Named-group answers were not addressed to the requesting machine, so a revoked device got nothing back.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: After a successful socket flush receipt during upgrade, the old process can stay alive indefinitely.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: Earlier fixes covered started-flush failure and producer-drain retry, but the successful-receipt path had no bounded wait before ending the stopped participant.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x upgrade flow, socket arm path, before the launcher client

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: The W3-H test case_1581 retries on any refusal instead of only the typed 409 wait.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: Retrying every refusal can hide real errors; only the typed 409 wait response should be retried and any other refusal should fail the test.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: A damaged .crblog or .orclog replay log can be overwritten instead of quarantined; restore and bound rules too loose.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: Review follow-up on replay logs: damaged files should be kept aside before any rewrite, and the restore and size-bound logic needs tightening.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: The test overlapping_startup_retries_cannot_exceed_the_send_bound flakes with 3 vs 2.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: Intermittent panic at issue1113_self_leave_rekey.rs:2988; the extra recorded call came from the test fixture's own detached asks, not from a startup send.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x named_groups tests on main, intermittent

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: A damaged .crblog or .orclog is overwritten without keeping a quarantine copy.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: replay_log.rs rewrites the damaged file, which breaks ADR 0085 rule 4 and loses evidence of the damage.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x replay logs that are damaged on disk

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Dormant upgrade inventory has no parser for Linux procfs process and mount evidence.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The host-inventory part of safe-apply upgrade needs to read process and mount info before it can attribute participants.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: The W3-H shim can still emit different traces because of a recheck wake gap and block_on event_interval.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: These differences are reported (D196) but do not fail the run, so the determinism check is weaker than it looks.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: cargo doc with warnings denied fails: unresolved intra-doc link start in tests/harness/src/daemon.rs.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The bare link [start] is not a path in that module, so cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps fails while the package docs command passes.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x workspace docs build with warnings as errors

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: A re-seat KeyPackage is not checked against the subject's agent key.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The re-seat acceptance rule should verify the KeyPackage the same way an ordinary join does.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Dormant upgrade inventory cannot parse /proc/<pid>/cmdline and environ bytes.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The producer needs process arguments and a few root environment values before it can collect launch context.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: TreeKEM catch-up spins the CPU and freezes Tokio virtual time by replaying the same event with no backoff.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: handle_treekem_catchup_response re-requests or replays a pending event at once with no throttle or stop condition except TTL, so tests with paused time hang until nextest kills them.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x named groups, TreeKEM catch-up on a fork-stranded joiner

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Home crash recovery adopts a shared group as Home and seals a commit that was never published.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: Recovery accepts any group whose policy equals GroupPolicy::home(owner), and a shared OwnerCertified group matches; other members then refuse the owner's next commit with PrevHashMismatch.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x owned install, Home provisioning after HOME_POINTER_SYNC_WAIT

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: The re-seat subject leaves containment before the keyed swap because the staged join runs in the live map.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The design says the staged join must happen in a staging record outside the live map, keeping the live record's marker, gate and refusals until the swap.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: A misspelled key in the exec ACL TOML is silently ignored, possibly giving a looser policy.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The connect ACL uses #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] so typos fail at load time, but the exec ACL structs did not.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: W3-H row H-S3-x times out at 300 s in CI and the determinism gate fails with no trace.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The case did not hang; virtual time kept moving but a request round waited out its old backoff, taking about 290 to 310 s on the runner.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Main CI red: the S3 W3-H shard goes over its deadline and an owner_recovery test races its own drive.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: Three symptoms with two code causes after recent merges.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x CI, W3-H S3 shard and owner_recovery test

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: S4 can seal a revocation before its revocation-store write is durable when the sidecar is memory-only.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The revocation-store write runs in a detached task that drops its errors, so S4 may act on a trigger not stored anywhere durable.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: CryptoExclusionV1 GSS keep-path trusts an uncommitted same-epoch secret without checking who sent it.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: A crypto-only exclusion could keep a group shared secret from any sender, not just the actor, in the same epoch.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x named groups, GSS crypto-only exclusion

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: GSS share hold still has gaps: MemberRemoved/Banned arms keep same-epoch secrets without a sender check.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: Other gaps: an E+1 share at the parent head and actorless holds from before upgrade.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x named groups, GSS share hold

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: The CI Test Suite job is killed with exit 143 while compiling x0x-test-harness.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The job dies (SIGTERM) before any test runs, on main and on PRs.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x CI Test Suite on GitHub Actions

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Revoked identities may still deliver messages over the raw-QUIC direct DM path.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The gossip DM path checks revocation per message, but it was unclear whether the direct QUIC path did the same.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x direct DMs over raw QUIC

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Task state endpoint returns Rust Debug-style text instead of JSON
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: A beta tester saw debug formatting rather than structured JSON.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: named_groups.json, which holds each group's shared_secret, is written world-readable (0644).
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The file is created with the default umask and then renamed into place, while the newer GSS share hold file is already 0600.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: The gossip DM path does not check machine-id revocation the way the direct path does.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x gossip DMs from revoked machines

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: The gossip PubSub dispatcher backs up and times out during fan-out bursts.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: A soak test showed dispatcher_timed_out=25 and recv_pump at 5815/10000; the direct DM path was unaffected.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x v0.28.0 under gossip fan-out bursts

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Joining a TreeKEM group over a command DM returns HTTP 400 for a random subset of nodes.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Common API calls give weak request validation and unclear error messages
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: A beta tester reported several small but frustrating validation and error-handling issues.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: x0xd panics with 'overflow when subtracting duration from instant' when started soon after Windows boots.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: Code computes a 5-minute cutoff by subtracting from Instant::now(); within 5 minutes of boot that underflows. Main culprit is saorsa-gossip-membership's maintenance loop, with call sites in ant-quic too.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0xd 0.29.0 on Windows, auto-started within 5 minutes of boot

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Key expiry is not enforced at runtime and some revocations are ignored over gossip and pubsub.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The runtime expiry gate was dead code, issuer revocations had no effect over gossip, and pubsub bypassed the RevocationSet.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Tailnet inbound forward ACL trusts an inferred agent_id, so rules only work per machine, not per agent.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The agent_id used for authorization was guessed rather than authenticated, collapsing access control to machine granularity.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Several small hardening gaps: off-loopback API warning, WS topic cap, stream double-count, eviction race.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x daemon API and connection handling

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: The Multi-Agent Integration CI job always hits its 20-minute timeout on PRs, failing with no test failure.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Machine-revocation binding relies on pubsub msg.sender being origin-authenticated, but this was undocumented.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The agent-to-machine binding is only stored when msg.verified and sender match; it is sound only if decode_v2 sets sender from the end-to-end signature, which needed auditing in saorsa-gossip.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Two x0xd instances on one machine cannot connect over 127.0.0.1
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The QUIC handshake times out after about 30 seconds.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Local dogfood smoke test fails: peer cannot post a group message or see its own message in cache.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: tests/e2e_dogfood_local.sh fails 2 of 19 checks deterministically on main.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x v0.31.0 with unpatched ant-quic master

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: A policy-rejected peer reconnects during its backoff window on CI runners.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x v0.31.x, ant-quic 0.27.30/0.27.31, slow CI runners

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: A cancelled tokio::fs write leaves .tmp files behind under load, failing a cleanup test.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: State recovery without checkpoints cannot confirm a peer actually served complete, current state.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: An earlier recovery fix accepted three known gaps for groups with no owner checkpoint, because closing them needed protocol work.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: proactive_reconnect_* and network_timeout tests fail under full-suite CPU contention.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x test suite under heavy CPU load

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Self-update replaces the binary but the restart can fail silently, leaving the daemon down.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x self-update on macOS, terminal-launched daemon

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: A testnet node becomes unreachable over SSH after fail2ban, breaking SSH-loop fleet monitoring.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.applies_when: x0x testnet fleet monitored via SSH

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Named-group admin-delete propagation integration tests fail intermittently.
https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.detail: The named_group_admin_delete_propagates_to_peer_after_creator_delete_409 family in tests/named_group_integration.rs flakes.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: The voice_call demo ignores its connection deadline and its E2E test is poorly paced.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: History search requires a scope and there is no way to list which scopes exist.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: docs/api-reference.md is missing the /history, /history/search and /diagnostics/history endpoints.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: ws_stalled_reader_fills_queue_and_closes_1013 fails: the daemon drops an in-flight /publish connection.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Proactive reconnect dials by bare address and drops the PeerId, so hole punching always fails.

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issue.problem: Group message send returns 200 and a msg_id even when it reached zero peers.
